newsitem.title: USA: RTRS-U.S. CREDIT OUTLOOK-Data seen fueling markets.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-U.S. CREDIT OUTLOOK-Data seen fueling markets.

text.p: Dealers expected busier U.S. credit markets in the coming holiday-shortened week, with a plethora of economic data releases scheduled.
"We'll probably see thin trading on Monday and Tuesday ahead of the holiday Wednesday, but after that things should really pick up," said Jonathan Basile, economist at HSBC Markets Inc.
Basile noted that while on the surface Tuesday appears to have the most data releases, it's the last day of the year and a short trading session," Basile said.

On Monday, November leading indicators and existing home sales data are slated for release. On Tuesday, investors will closely eye the BTM/Schroders and Redbook survey for clues on the strength of consumer spending during the holidays.

Tuesday also will see November new home sales data and the December Chicago Purchasing Managers index and December consumer confidence index. The Chicago index is often looked at as a precursor to the National Association of Purchasing Management's monthly index, which will be released on Thursday along with the November help wanted index and initial unemployment claims.

Economists surveyed by Reuters expected on average that the December NAPM survey would come in at 52.3, slightly less than Novewmber's reading of 52.7. A level above 50 is considered synonomous with economic growth.

Also on Thursday will be critical data on car and light truck sales, which were expected to remain strong as the industry closes out a year of strong sales growth. On Friday November construction spending will be released.
HSBC's Basile saw little reaction to Tuesday's data as most institutional money managers already have closed out their positions for the year.
"Of all the data coming out, the NAPM will have the most impact. It's the first national indicator for the month of December and in the past this number has moved the markets," said Basile.
In addition, the number will be released after the New Year's holiday, when most players are expected to be back at their desks, he said.

Basile noted that his firm is projecting a NAPM reading of 50.0, toward the low end of concensus estimates of a 52.3 level. The bond market, obviously, could rally sharply should the number come in below 50.0, Basile said.
Should the NAPM show an as-expected reading, it means that the manufacturing sector continues to enjoy growth, but is not expanding at an inflation-threatening pace, Basile said.
"It's important to look at the components of this number -- especially prices paid, prior deliveries and employment -- as these numbers themselves can move the markets," Basile said.
Late Friday the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was trading 20/32 higher at 99--16/32 to yield 6.54 percent. The 10-year was up 12/32 at 101-16/32 to yield 6.29 percent.
